column1: # This is a region policy, not a tokenizer implementation. Future tokenizers
# should assign a token to one of these regions, then use depth and mobility
# as the token's default learning/update behavior.
# byte_start/end    Inclusive UTF-8 byte range for the initial byte tokenizer.
# depth             0 = shallow/easy to move; 255 = deep/hard to move.
# mobility          Multiplier for future embedding/weight updates.
# notes             Why this region has its default behavior.

column6: Non-printing control bytes are shallow placeholders.
Whitespace is structural and should adapt quickly.
Remaining control bytes are shallow placeholders.
Common symbols and punctuation stay relatively mobile.
Separators and symbols stay relatively mobile.
Latin uppercase text is deep and changes slowly.
Delimiters and symbols stay relatively mobile.
Latin lowercase text is deep and changes slowly.
Delimiters and symbols stay relatively mobile.
UTF-8 continuation/extended bytes are moderately deep until a real tokenizer groups them.
Future padding token; should never become semantically anchored.
Future unknown-token fallback; adaptable but not fully shallow.
